# migration

Strangler-fig cutovers and breaking-change policy - every removal classified, dated and measured before consumers move.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-BREAK-001` — Removing an operation is always breaking (critical)

Clients compiled against a removed path/method fail with 404 at runtime — there is no compatible-deployment story, only coordinated consumer migration.

Remediation: Keep the operation and deprecate it (Deprecation/Sunset headers) until consumer inventory shows zero callers; removing without that evidence is a breaking release.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-BREAK-002` — Type and format changes are breaking (high)

`id: string -> integer` or `total: number -> string` silently breaks deserialization in typed clients and changes comparison semantics in untyped ones — the contract change is mechanical to detect.

Remediation: Add a new field with the new type and deprecate the old one, or cut a new version; never repurpose a field's type within a version.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-BREAK-003` — Tightening requirements is breaking (high)

Making an optional request field required, narrowing an enum, or shrinking a maxLength rejects requests that were valid — the failure is created entirely inside a released version.

Remediation: Only relax constraints within a version; tightening goes through deprecation (accept both, warn) or a new version.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-BREAK-004` — Response additions are safe; response removals are not (medium)

Tolerant readers ignore new fields; removing or renaming a response field breaks clients that bind it — the asymmetry is the whole rule.

Remediation: Evolve responses additively within a version; removals ride the deprecation window, never a minor bump.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-BREAK-005` — Deprecation is dated, announced and measurable (medium)

"Deprecated" without a sunset date and a consumer signal never finishes; RFC 9745 `Deprecation`/`Sunset` headers plus docs let consumers see the deadline and operators see the countdown.

Remediation: Emit `Deprecation: true` and `Sunset: <http-date>` on deprecated operations; announce in release notes; measure remaining traffic before removal.

Reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9745

### `AF-BREAK-006` — Semantic-version the contract, not the implementation (medium)

Consumers reason about the API surface, not internals — major bumps for breaking changes, minor for additions, patch for clarifications; reusing an implementation version confuses that signal.

Remediation: Version the contract document independently; bump `info.version` per the change class `diff contract` reports.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-BREAK-007` — Enum and constant additions are breaking for closed clients (medium)

Adding a value to an enum breaks clients that switch exhaustively or validate strictly — "additive" is only safe when the contract declares open/extensible semantics.

Remediation: Document enums as extensible (or use `x-extensible-enum`); treat additions to closed enums as breaking; deserializers tolerate unknown values.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md
